**DynaLM 0.2.0-beta.1: a beta pre-release.** It is verified on macOS on Apple Silicon. The Linux and Windows builds are preview. It is not a stable release, and it does not replace 0.1.7 as the latest release.

## Overview

DynaLM runs large language models locally, on the CPU or the GPU, as one program with no Python. It provides `dynalm run`, `chat` and `serve`, and an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API with streaming. This beta is for developers who want to try it on an Apple Silicon Mac and report what they find.

## Main improvements

- **Fast CPU path, accuracy against llama.cpp:**
  - Granite MoE expert weights are repacked as llama.cpp does: token agreement 93.8–94.4% → 99.96–100%; prefill +26%, decode +5% (Granite-3.1-1B-A400M).
  - Gemma's query is scaled before attention: 96.9–97.1% → 100%.
- **CPU scheduling:** the fast CPU path no longer uses the GPU's mixed-step settings. With 4 users, tokens/s +9.5–15% and 99th-percentile token gaps −53–58%.
- **Metal:**
  - GPU graphs are reordered for concurrency.
  - A one-line ggml patch removes false barriers.
  - A long-running server no longer slows down as its prefix cache fills the KV pool. The sparse attention used for this is automatic for steps whose span is at least 32× the context, up to 4,096 tokens.
  - Measured on Qwen2.5-1.5B with 16 users on a cache-filled 65,536-token pool: typical token gap 135.7 → 23.3 ms, tokens/s 98.6 → 152.3.
- **Benchmarks you can trust:**
  - Prompts are unique across benchmark points; earlier multi-user results reused prompts and are withdrawn.
  - Each engine's backend is verified from its own log.
  - The engine order is balanced.
  - Teacher-forced parity tooling compares against llama.cpp.
- **Tests:** sampling regression tests (temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, penalties) and a Metal dirty-pool attention test.

## Supported beta environment

| Artifact | Platform | Validation for this release |
|---|---|---|
| `dynalm-macos-arm64.tar.gz` | macOS on Apple Silicon, CPU and Metal | **Beta-verified** on one Apple M4 Pro: full test suite, parity with llama.cpp on eight models, DD-053 GPU accuracy, multi-user benchmarks |
| `dynalm-macos-x86_64.tar.gz` | macOS on Intel, CPU | **Preview:** built and tested in CI under Rosetta (model-free tests) |
| `dynalm-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, `dynalm-linux-arm64.tar.gz` | Linux, CPU | **Preview:** built, tested (model-free) and fresh-install checked in CI; not checked with real models |
| `dynalm-windows-x86_64.zip`, `dynalm-windows-arm64.zip` | Windows, CPU | **Preview:** as Linux |

- **Vulkan and CUDA are experimental.** They are built in CI, but Vulkan is tested only on a software GPU (lavapipe) and CUDA only built. The Vulkan archives are not attached to this pre-release.
- **CI and Metal:** CI's macOS runner has no Metal device, so Metal GPU behaviour was verified on the one physical Mac above.
- **Verified models** (GGUF):
  - Llama-3.1-8B Instruct Q8_0;
  - Qwen2.5-0.5B and 1.5B Instruct Q4_K_M;
  - Qwen3-0.6B Q8_0, Qwen3-4B and 8B Q4_K_M;
  - Gemma-3-1B Q4_K_M;
  - Granite-3.1-1B-A400M Q4_K_M.

  Other models and quantizations are preview.

## Performance and accuracy

All results are from one Apple M4 Pro (24 GB, macOS 26.7, AC power).

**Accuracy against llama.cpp** (same GGUF files, teacher-forced, 10 × 512 tokens of wikitext-2):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| CPU next-token agreement | 99.96–100%, identical perplexity |
| Metal next-token agreement | 99.80–100% |
| Metal greedy text | identical on 4 of 4 prompts per model |
| DD-053 GPU accuracy | passes on all eight models |

This measures agreement with llama.cpp, not answer quality.

**Speed against llama.cpp's server** (Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M, Llama-3.1-8B Q8_0; 512-token prompts, 128 output tokens, 2,048 tokens of context per user; medians over 3 rounds):

A difference is "confirmed" only when all 3 rounds agree beyond ±10% and both engines varied by 10% or less. llama.cpp's multi-user results varied by up to about 30% between rounds, so several differences are not confirmed.

| Device and load | Result | Confirmed? |
|---|---|---|
| Metal, one user | about the same speed | parity on the 8B models; the others inconclusive |
| Metal, 16 users: total tokens/s | 0.71–0.78× (llama.cpp ahead) | yes, 3 of 4 models |
| Metal, 16 users: 99th-percentile token gaps | 7–10× shorter with DynaLM | yes for the 8B models |
| Metal, 16 users: first token | 2.1–3.3× sooner (median) | no, on all four models |
| Metal, 4 users: 99th-percentile token gaps | longer with DynaLM (0.19–0.30×) | no (consistent direction) |
| CPU, one user: time per token | 0.77–0.97× llama.cpp's (the CPU builds differ: llama.cpp native with Accelerate, DynaLM portable) | yes, 3 of 4 models |

**DynaLM is not faster than llama.cpp overall.**

## Known limitations

- Verified on one physical Mac and eight models. Linux and Windows inference with real models has not been validated for this release.
- **16 users on Metal:** total throughput is 0.71–0.78× llama.cpp's.
- **4 users:** 99th-percentile token gaps are longer than llama.cpp's.
- **CPU decode:** 0.77–0.97× llama.cpp's speed.
- **Memory limits are enforced at load.** Llama-3.1-8B Q8_0 with 16 users × 4,096 tokens on a 24 GB Mac is refused (8.0 GiB of KV against 6.9 GiB available); use `--ctx 57024` or less, or `--kv q8_0`.
- **Granite MoE on the CPU** uses about 0.7 GB more memory for its repacked expert weights.
- **Sparse attention** keeps a cache-filled Metal server fast for contexts up to 4,096 tokens only; longer contexts still slow down. Vulkan, CUDA and the CPU path don't use it.
- **Vulkan and CUDA are experimental.** Some models (YaRN RoPE scaling; MoE on CUDA) run on the CPU.

## Installation

From this release (macOS on Apple Silicon):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dynalm-project/dynalm/main/scripts/install.sh | sh -s -- --version v0.2.0-beta.1
dynalm --version   # DynaLM   0.2.0-beta.1
```

The installer without `--version` installs the latest **stable** release (0.1.7). Each archive is listed in `SHA256SUMS` and carries signed build provenance: `gh attestation verify <file> --repo dynalm-project/dynalm`. To build from source, see `docs/build.md`.

## Changes and compatibility

- **`--backend native-cpu` is no longer available.** It stops with an error naming the replacement:
  - `--backend cpu` for the fast CPU kernels;
  - `--mode exact` for DynaLM's own DD-053 CPU kernels.

  Configuration files with `runtime.device: native-cpu` need `runtime.device: cpu` and `runtime.mode: exact`.
- **`DYNACORE_GPU_SPARSE`:** `0` restores the previous dense-only Metal attention, `1` forces sparse attention.
- **`dynalm benchmark --prompt-base N`:** new option.
- **No Docker image:** this pre-release does not update `ghcr.io/dynalm-project/dynalm:cpu`.
